title: Korean Language and Culture BA
notes:
Language Mastery: Rigorous training in modern spoken and written Korean, with opportunities to study hanja (classical Chinese characters used in Korea) and premodern Korean texts, offering deeper insights into Korea’s linguistic and intellectual traditions.
Interdisciplinary Exploration: A broad array of courses on Korean literature, film, history, popular culture, and sociolinguistics. Courses are taught both in translation and in Korean, enabling students to engage critically with Korea’s dynamic cultural and historical landscapes.
Regional and Historical Context: The program situates Korea within the broader East Asian context, while fostering an in-depth understanding of Korea’s unique historical experiences—including its encounters with colonialism, national division, war, and rapid modernization—through comparative and interdisciplinary perspectives.

requirements.title: Elementary Korean
requirements.notes:
Students with prior experience in language, either by study or heritage learning, are required to take a placement exam and begin at the level determined by the exam.
If you have already taken this exam, reach out to your advisor to update your status.
Students can also place out of Elementary Korean A/B with the placement exam milestone.
